title: Contention-aware prefill reservation and kernel hop-steer for paged-attention
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Paged attention workloads show bursty access to sparse KV pages. Under multi-tenant pressure this causes repeated small evictions and hot-slot contention during prefill, which in turn creates decode stalls and tail latency spikes. Current reservation heuristics are coarse (per-shard or global soft reserve) and the default kernel fallback path tends to either overcommit memory or serialize decodes, worsening 95p token latency for interactive workloads.

Goal:
Introduce a contention-aware micro-reservation allocator and a complementary kernel hop-steer policy that reduces prefill-induced stalls and eviction churn while preserving throughput. The feature should be safe to enable behind a runtime flag and rolled out as a canary to Dedicated pools before wider release.

Design overview (high level):
1) Micro-reservation allocator (thrift):
   - Instead of global soft reserves, allocate tenant-scoped micro-reservations (configurable quantum, default 4-8 pages) on prefill admission.
   - Reservations are ephemeral credits with a decay window; credits are charged when pages are touched and refunded if not used within the window.
   - Admission score combines: tenant request priority, recent reuse probability (lightweight bloom + touch-frequency), and current shard contention metric (moving-average of concurrent prefill attempts).
   - When contention is high, the allocator favors high-score requests and issues a backoff token to low-score requests rather than immediately evicting resident pages.

2) Contention-driven eviction softening:
   - Eviction policy temporarily increases eviction hysteresis for pages with high reuse probability to avoid oscillation under transient bursts.
   - Introduce a short "gentle-stall" path where a request may wait (bounded, e.g., 4-8ms) for a micro-reservation to free up instead of triggering an aggressive eviction. This amortizes eviction cost across concurrent requests.

3) Kernel hop-steer (decode fast-path steering):
   - When a prefill would otherwise block decode due to missing KV pages, select a hop kernel: a lightweight, small-window kernel variant that performs partial attention on available context and issues asynchronous fetches for missing pages.
   - The hop kernel reduces stall length by returning a partial token batch quickly and allowing the main kernel to finish once pages arrive, reducing tail latency at a small throughput cost.
   - Kernel selection rules: consider sequence length, missing page fraction, and estimated fetch latency. Default heuristic: if missing fraction < 30% and fetch latency > 2ms, prefer hop kernel.

4) Decode touchdown scheduler:
   - Schedule decode bursts to align with expected prefill completion times. The scheduler uses expiry estimates from the micro-reservation allocator and kernel completion time predictors to avoid schedule collisions that exacerbate contention.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Implement micro-reservation data structures + admission scoring. Add metrics (reservation grants, deny rate, contention metric). Add unit tests for credit accounting.
- Week 2: Implement eviction hysteresis toggle and gentle-stall path. Integrate with existing eviction codepaths.
- Week 3: Prototype hop kernel selection and implement a minimal hop kernel integration point in the runtime (config guarded).
- Week 4: Add decode touchdown scheduler and integrate with request router. Run synthetic load tests and compare to baseline.
- Week 5: Canary deploy to one Dedicated pool; collect metrics and iterate.

Observability and metrics to add:
- reservation.grants, reservation.denials, reservation.avg_credit_lifetime
- contention.window_concurrent_prefill (moving avg)
- eviction.hysteresis_hits, eviction.churn_rate
- kernel.selection.counts (main vs hop), kernel.hop_latency_reduction_pXX
- tail token latency (p50/p95/p99) for prefill-heavy routes

Acceptance criteria:
- 95p prefill-induced token latency reduces by at least 30% in synthetic multi-tenant sparse workloads (baseline -> target: e.g., 230ms -> <160ms).
- Eviction churn (evictions/sec for hot pages) decreases by at least 25% under the same load.
- No throughput regression > 5% for steady-state long-sequence generative workloads.
- All new heuristics gated behind runtime flags and covered by unit + e2e tests.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for credit accounting, decay, and denial/backoff tokens.
- Offline simulator: model synthetic tenanted touch traces to validate allocation fairness and churn.
- Perf harness: run 10k-request multi-tenant sparse workload across baseline and new allocator in Dedicated canary; collect metrics.
- Safety: blackhole flag to disable hop kernel selection and emergency toggle for reservation behavior.

Risks and tradeoffs:
- Hop kernel increases code complexity and slightly reduces raw throughput for some patterns; mitigation via conservative default heuristics and canarying.
- Mis-calibrated decay windows could starve low-priority tenants; mitigate by adding a slow-growing fairness boost.
- Extra metrics and bookkeeping add overhead; we will measure CPU/memory cost and tune quantum sizes to keep overhead <2% at baseline load.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature behind runtime flags; internal canary in a small Dedicated pool (control vs experimental).
2) 1-2 week observation window; tune heuristics.
3) Gradual ramp to 10% then 50% of Dedicated capacity.
4) Post-rollout: monitor p99/p95 token latency, eviction churn, and reserve grant/deny ratios.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/987654321/Contention+aware+prefill+allocator (draft)
- Simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prefill-sim/pull/12
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3142

Notes:
- This ticket focuses on the allocator and kernel steering integration; follow-up tickets will explore cross-shard cooperative prefill and hardware-specific kernel tuning for hop kernels.
